senses.gloss: m. (b. h.; = כבכב, v. כבב) [rounded, globe,] star, planet.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1:6">Y. Ber. I, 2ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ אחד ודאי יום</he> as long as one star only is visible, it is surely day-time.
<cite ref="Horayot 10a:19">Hor. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>כ׳ אחד יש ועולה וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) there is a certain star (comet) which appears once in seventy years.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 100:9">Gen. R. s. 100</cite> <he>עשרה כוכבים בקשו לאבד כ׳ אחד</he> ten stars (sons of Jacob) desired to destroy one star (Joseph); a. fr.—Pl. <he>כּוֹכָבִים</he>, <he>כֹּכָ׳</he>.

<cite ref="Berakhot 10a:14">Ber. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>כ׳ ומזלות</he> stars and planets; a. fr.—<he>עובד כ׳</he>, <he>עובד כ׳ ומזלות</he> (abbr. <he>עו״כ</he>, <he>עכו״ם</he>), <he>עבודת כ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="P00013"><he>עָבַד</he></cite>, <cite ref="P00026"><he>עֲבוֹדָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sukkah 22b:8">Succ. 22ᵇ</cite>; Y. ib. II, beg. 22ᵈ <he>כּוֹכְבֵי חמה</he> scintillations of the sun as seen through the covering of the festive booth.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 1053:7">Yalk. Esth. 1053</cite> <he>כ׳ חנגה</he>, v. <cite ref="K00250">next w.</cite>
